title: Regional edge offload strategy — arch retrospective
content:
Meeting: Regional Edge Offload Strategy — Architecture Retrospective
Date: 2025-01-10
Attendees: Anika Patel (owner), Diego Ramos, Hannah Lee, Owen Park, Sarah Ng, Marcus Liu
Location: Zoom + #platform-eng-sync thread
Goal: Review the proposed strategy for opportunistic inference offload to regional edge nodes, capture design decisions, unresolved risks, and an actionable rollout plan.

Background:
- Problem: For latency-sensitive customers in APAC/EU we want to reduce tail latency by routing some inference traffic to regional edge sites (lightweight inference points) without losing SLOs or increasing cost excessively. Edge nodes are constrained (memory, disk, CPU) and may have intermittent connectivity to control plane.
- Previous work: quick prototype for local quantized variants (spike test in Sprint 40). Related artifacts: RFC-2024-11-Edge-Offload, runtime PR #4821.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Non-goal: full parity with hosted model catalog features (no full console integration on day-0).
- Constraint: edge nodes can only hold quantized model variants (8-bit / 4-bit) and a subset of tokenizer vocab to save RAM.
- Constraint: network egress is metered in several regions and may be expensive for large embedding outputs.
- Constraint: model provenance & signature verification must remain intact for audit/compliance.

Design options reviewed (summary):
1) Pull-model start: Edge node pulls compressed model artifacts from regional artifact store on deploy. Signed binaries verified via model-artifact-signing. Local cache + LRU eviction.
   - Pros: simpler control-plane changes, easier provenance checks.
   - Cons: cold start time for large models; storage footprint at edge.

2) Push-model streaming: Control plane streams delta updates (quantized shards) and applies patches to edge runtime, with background prefetching based on traffic heuristics.
   - Pros: faster updates, smaller initial transfer for common models.
   - Cons: more complex; needs robust transactional apply to avoid partial state.

3) Hybrid: keep a tiny canonical runtime on edge with runtime-native model adaptation (model slicing + on-demand shard fetch). Metadata stored centrally; fetch only needed KV and attention weight shards.
   - Pros: minimizes on-disk model size, good for hot prefixes.
   - Cons: requires new shard layout format and richer runtime changes.

Security & compliance discussion:
- Must integrate with existing KMS signing flow; edge nodes verify model signatures before activation. Proposal: include a local certificate store for root keys and periodic CRL sync from control plane.
- For private deployments, customer-managed HSM is required; we will surface a flag in Private config to disable automatic artifact fetch and rely on operator-provided artifacts.
- Telemetry must not leak PII; for privacy regions we will sample only perf metrics and use hashed model ids.

Telemetry and observability:
- Required metrics: local inference p50/p95/p99, kv-cache-hit-rate, model-load-latency, disk-evictions, network-fetch-latency, signed-verification-failures.
- Alerts: model-load-latency > 10s (P1), signed-verification-failure rate > 0.1% (P0), sustained p99 increase > 30% vs baseline (P1).
- Add a dashboard tile: regional-offload — showing proportion of traffic offloaded, per-model success rate, and cost delta.

Performance modeling (back-of-envelope):
- Edge nodes expected to reduce regional tail latency by 20–50% for single-turn completion workloads for short contexts (<512 tokens).
- Cost tradeoff: per-token compute cost at edge is slightly higher due to smaller batch efficiency; expected break-even if at least 30% of traffic is latency sensitive (SLA-driven) vs cross-region serve.

Compatibility & correctness:
- Conversation/context consistency: edge nodes will keep short-term KV cache (per-session) but will not have long conversation history beyond configured retention (default 1k tokens). For long conversation histories read-from-origin fallback is required.
- Determinism: quantized models produce small distributional shifts. We will document expected delta and provide a QA harness for customer-facing consistency tests (prompt suite).

Testing plan:
- Unit: validation of model signature verification, artifact integrity checks.
- Integration: staged tests with regional canary (EU-west, APAC-southeast) in a dedicated namespace with synthetic workloads (short chat, long chat, streaming).
- Perf: load tests for concurrency 1–64, varying batch window; track p99 and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Regression: run the prompt-suite against quantized variants and compare hallucination rate and semantic similarity metrics.

Rollout plan (recommended):
- Phase 0: Internal dogfood only. Deploy in two regions, internal beta customers. Duration 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: Customer opt-in (SaaS seats with latency SLAs). Canary at 5% traffic per region for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2: Adaptive rollout up to 30% for eligible traffic, with automatic fallback to regional-hosted model on specific error triggers.
- Phase 3: General availability (GA) after 8–12 weeks of stable telemetry and resolved regressions.

Fallback & rollback triggers (auto):
- If signed-verification-failures > 0.05% for 1m window -> automatic disable edge offload for that model and trigger an alert.
- If p99 latency increases > 2x baseline for 10m -> rollback to origin routing.
- If semantic-regression-delta on prompt-suite exceeds threshold -> mark model as degraded and deprecate edge variant.

Decisions made during meeting:
- Chosen approach: Hybrid (option 3) as primary path but implement Pull-model as a fast-follower to enable quicker customer trials. Hybrid gives better cold-start behavior for hot prefixes and minimizes storage in constrained sites.
- Must sign and version shard manifests; manifest format v1 agreed.
- Telemetry design: implement minimal tile and three alerts defined above before Phase 1.
- Private deployments: operator-provided artifacts only (no auto-fetch) for initial GA.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle tokenizer subset drift across model versions? (Hannah to prototype tokenizer fallback logic)
- Bandwidth cost unpredictability in some APAC regions — need a cost limiter. (Finance to provide regional rate card estimate: Finance ticket JIRA-FN-498)
- Complexity of maintaining parity between quantized model outputs and mainline hosted models — need clear SLO for semantic deviation.

Action items (owner — due):
- Build shard manifest schema v1 and spec doc — Owen Park — 2025-01-17
- Prototype tokenizer subset fallback and report edge-case errors — Hannah Lee — 2025-01-24
- Add telemetry dashboard tiles + alert rules to staging — Diego Ramos — 2025-01-20
- Implement model-signature verification in edge runtime (unit + integ tests) — Marcus Liu — 2025-01-31
- Run prompt-suite on 4-bit / 8-bit quantized variants and produce comparison report — Anika Patel — 2025-02-07

Notes & references:
- See RFC-2024-11-Edge-Offload for initial requirements and experiment data.
- Runtime PR #4821 contains initial shard-fetch plumbing; will iterate based on Owen's manifest schema.
- Related: model-artifact-signing-and-provenance-rfc-notes (platform-engineering) for signature flow.

Next sync: 2025-01-24 (standup to review prototypes and first telemetry curves).

Appendix (quick decisions we deferred):
- Decision deferred: whether to support live model hotpatch streaming at GA (deferred to post-GA).
- Decision deferred: exact default retention for conversation KV on edge (TBD after perf tests).

End of notes.
